title: fanoutqa: Identify the architects of five historical landmarks: the Eiffel Tower, the Sydney Opera House, the Taj Mahal, the Empire State Building, and the Parthenon. (9079b63f36e57692)

chat_history.content: Identify the architects of five historical landmarks: the Eiffel Tower, the Sydney Opera House, the Taj Mahal, the Empire State Building, and the Parthenon.

content.content:
The user asks to identify the architects of five historical landmarks: Eiffel Tower, Sydney Opera House, Taj Mahal, Empire State Building, Parthenon. Provide names.

We need to give: Eiffel Tower - engineer Gustave Eiffel (architect Maurice Koechlin? Actually chief engineer Eiffel). Usually credited to engineer Gustave Eiffel, design by Maurice Koechlin and Emile Nouguier. The architect was Stephen Sauvestre (architect for decorative aspects). But commonly known as Gustave Eiffel. We'll provide.

Sydney Opera House - architect Jørn Utzon.

Taj Mahal - architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori (chief architect). Also mentions Mughal emperor Shah Jahan commissioned, but architect is Ustad Ahmad Lahori.

Empire State Building - architect William F. Lamb of Shreve, Lamb & Harmon.

Parthenon - architects Ictinus and Callicrates, with sculptor Phidias overseeing artistic aspects.

Answer accordingly.

content:
Here are the primary designers/architects most commonly credited with each of the five landmarks:

| Landmark | Primary Architect(s) / Designer(s) | Brief Note |
|----------|------------------------------------|------------|
| **Eiffel Tower (Paris, France)** | **Gustave Eiffel** (chief engineer) – design work was carried out by his senior engineers **Maurice Koechlin** and **Émile Nouguier**, with the architectural embellishments added by **Stephen Sauvestre**. | The tower was built for the 1889 Exposition Universelle; Eiffel’s firm oversaw the entire project. |
| **Sydney Opera House (Sydney, Australia)** | **Jørn Utzon** (Danish architect) | Utzon won the 1957 international design competition; his iconic sail‑like shells were realized between 1959‑1973. |
| **Taj Mahal (Agra, India)** | **Ustad Ahmad Lahori** (chief architect) – assisted by a team of Mughal artisans and craftsmen. | Commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan (1628‑1653) as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal; construction began in 1632. |
| **Empire State Building (New York City, USA)** | **William F. Lamb** (lead architect) of the firm **Shreve, Lamb & Harmon Associates** | Designed in 1930 and completed in 1931; Lamb’s design emphasized a sleek, setback “wedding‑cake” silhouette. |
| **Parthenon (Athens, Greece)** | **Ictinus** and **Callicrates** (architects) – with sculptor **Phidias** supervising the decorative program. | Constructed 447‑432 BC on the Acropolis as a temple to Athena; the architects coordinated the Doric design and overall layout. |

These names are the individuals most widely recognized in historical and architectural scholarship as the creators (or chief designers) of each monument.
